clue.text: Power cross round back of defenders before clinical header

indicators.note: round says the mule's letters go around what follows

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a donkey and a horse

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter, so take the end of defenders
a header is the top letter, so take the start of clinical

explanation.surface: A football match report: a powerful cross from the back before a clinical header into the net.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture hides a hybrid animal: 'round' puts S and C, joined by 'before', inside MULE.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscle is strength or force, as in financial or political muscle, so it can stand for power.

clue.text: Parking fee causing madness in cows?

parts.note: moo is the sound cows make
rage is madness or fury

explanation.surface: A charge for parking blamed for driving cattle mad.
explanation.walkthrough: Cow madness reads as MOO-RAGE; the parking is of a boat, not a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorage is a charge for mooring a vessel, a fee for parking a boat.

clue.text: Talk about a barbarian when 16 down with this mug!

parts.words: Talk about a barbarian when 16 down with this
parts.note: the girl's name at 16 down followed by this word, spoken, sounds like a word for an uncultured person

explanation.surface: Someone sneering at a boor while drinking from a beer mug.
explanation.walkthrough: PHYLLIS (16 down) plus STEIN, said together, sounds like PHILISTINE, a barbarian.
explanation.definitionFit: A stein is a large earthenware beer mug of German origin.

clue.text: Unit of luminance, centre light seen in extremes of light

indicators.note: seen in says the amber is placed within the outer letters
extremes are the ends, the first and last letters of the second light

parts.note: amber is the middle light of a traffic signal

explanation.surface: A technical note on brightness and the middle lamp of traffic signals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes of light' gives L and T; amber sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambert is an old unit of luminance, named after the scientist Johann Lambert.

clue.text: King, perhaps, outlining an untrue story

indicators.note: outlining means going round the edge of, so card's letters surround the word an

parts.note: a king is one example of a playing card

explanation.surface: A monarch caught spreading a false tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King, perhaps' looks like a monarch, but kings are also found in a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A canard is a false report or hoax spread to deceive, so it is an untrue story.

clue.text: Trouble seen under idiot: attack!

indicators.note: in a down clue, under puts the trouble word below the idiot

parts.note: an ass is a fool
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A rallying cry: trouble spotted beneath a fool, so charge!
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the imperative verb, matching the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to attack violently, so the command assail! means attack!

clue.text: One's bald head at first appearing stupid, very pale on top

indicators.note: appearing stupid suggests muddled, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the word one's, its S kept as a letter

indicators.note: at first takes the first letter of head

explanation.surface: A bald man looks silly, his pate shining very pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing stupid' rearranges ONES, BALD and H (the first letter of head, by 'at first').
explanation.definitionFit: Ash blonde hair is a very light greyish blond, a pale colour on the head.

clue.text: One country starts to excavate, digging up old coins

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the whole run is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
Iran is a country

indicators.note: starts to takes the first letters of excavate and digging

explanation.surface: A nation begins excavating and turns up ancient coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' gives E and D; 'up' reverses IIRANED, the whole run.
explanation.definitionFit: Denarii were silver coins of ancient Rome, so they are old coins.

clue.text: Having turned back, do seek run to get off the mark

indicators.note: turned means twisted round, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricketer reverses and dashes to score at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' rearranges BACK, DO, SEEK and RUN. In cricket a duck is a score of nought, so to break it is to score a first run.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking one's duck is scoring a first run in cricket, so it is an idiom for getting off the mark.

clue.text: "Night and Day" was his food and drink

parts.note: cole is an old name for cabbage and its relatives, so a vegetable food
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A songwriter whose famous song is paired with what he ate and drank.
explanation.walkthrough: COLE (cabbage, kale and the like) is a rare word; PORTER is a dark British beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole Porter, the American songwriter, wrote the standard Night and Day for the 1932 musical Gay Divorce.

clue.text: Cherry around thirteen miles? So inch out

parts.note: a marathon is about twenty-six miles, so roughly thirteen miles is half the word marathon, its first four letters

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of so and inch are rearranged

explanation.surface: A runner's half-distance musing on cherries and shortfalls of an inch.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the trick: about thirteen miles is half a marathon, so half the word MARATHON, MARA. 'out' rearranges SO INCH into SCHINO.
explanation.definitionFit: A maraschino is a cherry preserved in maraschino liqueur, the sort used to garnish cocktails.

clue.text: Hand once named as brave

parts.note: a paw is a hand, informally
née introduces a former name, typically a woman's maiden name

explanation.surface: A card hand with an old name being called courageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave' is a noun here: a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave is a Native American warrior, and a Pawnee is a member of a people of the Great Plains.

clue.text: Sick topless girl after a kiss on the armpit

indicators.note: after says the following pieces come behind the a and kiss in the answer

parts.note: X is the conventional symbol for a kiss at the end of a letter
ill means sick

indicators.note: topless means losing the first letter of the girl's name

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A tabloid line about an unwell, topless girl getting a kiss on the armpit.
explanation.walkthrough: The racy picture is misdirection: 'topless' is a deletion and 'on the armpit' is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Axillary is the anatomical adjective for the axilla, the armpit, so it means located on or relating to that spot.

clue.text: How long might one be expecting process to go, a president introducing one?

definitions.text: How long might one be expecting

indicators.note: introducing means bringing one in among the reworked letters
to process something is to work it over, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A question about how long a procedure takes once a new president is brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'process' rearranges TO GO and A PRESIDENT; 'introducing' sets I among them. 'expecting' means pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: A gestation period is the length of pregnancy, the time during which one is expecting a baby.

clue.text: Miniature person getting from A to B in the end

indicators.note: in says the altered person word goes inside the end word

parts.note: a tail is the end of something

indicators.note: getting from A to B says the letter A in the person word becomes B

parts.note: a human is a person

explanation.surface: A tiny traveller finally getting from one place to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting from A to B' reads as a journey but is a letter swap inside the person word; 'in' then sets that inside the end word.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbnail is a small picture or sketch, and a miniature is likewise a tiny painting.

clue.text: What's designed to stabilise an Austrian state, right behind Libya, oddly

indicators.note: behind places the right abbreviation at the end, after the Libya letters

parts.note: Tirol (Tyrol) is a state of western Austria

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of Libya, first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A geopolitical scheme to steady an Austrian region by putting it behind Libya.
explanation.walkthrough: TIROL is the German spelling of Tyrol; 'oddly' takes L, B, A from Libya.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti-roll bar is a car suspension part that keeps the body steady when cornering.

clue.text: Stop promotion

definitions.meaning: to block up a hole or gap, as with a stopper
a piece of publicity, such as a mention for a book on a chat show

explanation.definitionFit: A plug seals a hole, and to plug a product is to advertise it, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Girl's ridiculous sauce, upside down

indicators.note: in a down clue, upside down reverses the whole run of letters

parts.note: silly means ridiculous
HP is a brown sauce sold in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone calls a girl's sauce bottle ludicrous because it is upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: HP Sauce is a well-known British brown sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Phyllis is a girl's name.

clue.text: Parrot catching, for example, the bowling strategy

indicators.note: catching means holding, so the parrot's letters hold the next pieces

parts.note: a lory is a small brightly coloured parrot

explanation.surface: A parrot catching a ball, as in a cricket strategy.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, leg theory was bowling at the batter's body with fielders packed on the leg side, the basis of the 1930s Bodyline tactic.
explanation.definitionFit: Leg theory is a cricket bowling plan aimed at the leg side with a packed field, so it is a strategy.

clue.text: French shop stocking head of squid over duck sauce

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the shop on top of the duck
stocking means keeping as stock, so the shop holds the next letter

parts.note: a tabac is a French tobacconist

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of squid

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, written O

explanation.surface: A French store stocks squid alongside duck in a hot sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: A tabac is a French tobacconist.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabasco is a fiery red pepper sauce from Louisiana.

clue.text: See 15
See 13
Dense food dry, a beer is drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests being thrown about, so the letters of dry, a and beer are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dry beer is downed alongside something stodgy to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is drunk' rearranges DRY A BEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye bread is a heavy, close-textured loaf, a dense kind of food.

clue.text: By restricting flow, it keeps one dry

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the letters of by enclose the flow word

parts.note: to roll is to flow, as a river rolls along

explanation.surface: A dam that limits water flow keeps the land dry.
explanation.walkthrough: BROLLY is British slang for an umbrella; the surface pictures a dam, but 'By' is used as its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A brolly is an umbrella, which keeps its holder dry in the rain.

clue.text: Round component's modern style

parts.note: the circular letter O looks like a round
a part is a component

explanation.surface: A circular piece in a contemporary design.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is a 1960s movement of abstract optical illusion, a modern artistic style.

clue.text: Two hundred failures, unfortunately very little entertainment

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two hundred is CC

explanation.surface: Two hundred flops mean a show that hardly entertains anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges CC and FAILURES. 'very little' is literal: the performers are tiny insects.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea circus is a sideshow of performing fleas, entertainment on a minute scale.

clue.text: The father of pop?

parts.note: an Aramaic word meaning father, used of God in the New Testament, is also the name of a Swedish pop group

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark joins two senses: a biblical word for father, and a famous 1970s Swedish band.
explanation.definitionFit: Abba is an Aramaic term for father and also the Swedish group behind Dancing Queen, a pillar of pop.

clue.text: Old coins from Madrid I lost on the way back

indicators.note: on the way back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A traveller lost old money in Madrid on the return trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' signals the hidden run in MADRID I LOST, and 'on the way back' reverses IDILOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Solidi were gold coins of the late Roman Empire, so they are old coins.
